2789:
(a) No person shall use or occupy the streets to operate a utility, within Macon-Bibb County, including but not limited to the operation of railroads, street railways, urban transportation companies, electric or light power companies, gas companies, steam-heat companies, telecommunications or cable companies, or water companies without first having obtained a franchise agreement from Macon-Bibb County.
(b) Any person who seeks the right to exercise a franchise in Macon-Bibb County which contemplates or makes necessary the erection and construction of any building, poles, wires, conduits, tracks or other similar equipment, in, upon or over any street located in Macon-Bibb County, shall file a written petition therefor. The petition shall contain an accurate description of the rights sought to be secured, and shall be accompanied by a plat showing the exact location or proposed location of the building, poles, tracks and the like, together with all streets upon or over which it is sought to exercise the franchise.
(c) The petition shall be filed with the clerk of commission accompanied by a deposit sufficient to cover the cost of advertising the petition as provided in this chapter, and no petition shall be received, filed, or presented to the commission until the full amount of the cost of the advertising shall have been first paid to the clerk of commission, who shall keep a record thereof. The petition shall be advertised in the official newspaper of Macon-Bibb County at least once a week for four weeks before it shall be considered by the city council commission or any committee thereof.
(d) Existing franchises from the City of Macon and/or Bibb County shall continue in force and effect in Macon-Bibb County until such time as said franchises expire, are renewed, or new franchises are issued by the commission.
(e) (1) It shall be unlawful for any person, except a franchisee, to place any telephone, telegraph or other wires, cables, conduits, pipes, or other equipment used for telecommunications, cable or other communications purposes upon, under or above the rights-of-way of any street without first having obtained an access agreement with Macon-Bibb County as allowed by state law. Such agreement shall specify the name of the street involved, the purpose for which the wire, pipe, cable or conduit is run, the type and length of wire, cable, pipe, or conduit to be run, the extent of the construction to be performed, and the time allowed for performance of the work. The installation of such telephone or telegraph wires, cables or conduits shall be done by a licensed contractor and such work shall be done in a workmanlike manner in accordance with any specifications provided in regulations adopted by the Macon-Bibb County engineer.
(2) Such access agreement shall be granted only for a specified portion of particular streets and shall provide for compensation to Macon-Bibb County in an amount not to exceed the maximum amounts specified or allowed by state or federal law.
2790:
(a) The words "public utility," for the purposes of this section, shall include but shall not be limited to water lines, gas lines, sewer lines, pipelines, telephone lines, power lines, telecommunication cables, conduits and every other structure or device which by physical or electronic means conveys energy or substance, whether overhead or underground, along with supporting pedestals, poles and equipment.
(b) No person shall install or relocate any utility without compliance with this section.
(c) Before any public utility may be installed or relocated, application for a permit shall be made to the engineer of Macon-Bibb County. The application for the permit shall contain the name and address of the applicant, a description of the location and nature of the public utility and such other information as the engineer may reasonably require. The engineer shall issue a permit for such installation or relocation which conforms to this chapter.
(d) The Macon-Bibb County engineer shall not approve any permit for the installation or relocation of an underground utility where the topmost portion of the conduit, cable, wire, pipe or other feature is less than 30 inches below the surface of the ground at the time of completion of the installation, nor shall the engineer permit installation or relocation of an overhead utility where any aboveground fixture, pole, pedestal, or feature is not behind the ditch in a rural section, or behind the curb in an urban section, upon completion.
(e) The engineer may make other reasonable requirements governing the installation or relocation as shall be necessary to provide reasonable protection to the utility and to persons and property, both public and private. No public utility, once installed, shall be relocated without application for and receipt of a permit, and then only so long as its relocation meets the location requirements outlined in subsection (d).
(f) Whenever any person shall desire to change the conditions which were present at the time a public utility was appropriately installed (by grading, installing a driveway or private street, piping a ditch, etc.) in such fashion as to reduce the depth of an underground utility, or to otherwise necessitate relocation of any public utility, such person shall make prior arrangements for such relocation so as to comply with the location parameters required by subsection (d). The cost of such relocation shall be borne by the person desiring to change the conditions which would necessitate a relocation, unless otherwise agreed between the person and the utility; provided, however, that whenever it shall become requisite to relocate a utility by reason of necessity to grade, widen or otherwise improve a public roadway, drainage system, or sidewalk then in existence, the cost of such relocation of the utility shall be the expense of the owner of the utility unless otherwise provided in the franchise agreement.
(g) Any person who is installing an overhead wire or cable requiring an access agreement across a street or highway shall at all times maintain a minimum 18-foot clearance above the surface of such street or highway.
(h) Any person who is installing an underground wire, cable, pipe, or conduit requiring an access agreement shall also comply with the provisions of chapter 18 which deals with excavations into a public street.
(i) The Macon-Bibb County engineer shall be authorized to require a holder of an access agreement to relocate their wire, cable or conduit if such relocation is a public necessity. The engineer may also require an overhead wire or cable to be relocated if the street involved should convert from an overhead telephone system to an underground telephone system.
2791:
(a) Telegraph, telephone, and electric poles shall only be erected in a manner that best promotes pedestrian mobility and the work shall be done under the supervision of and subject to the approval of the Macon-Bibb County engineer. On failure of any company or person to locate these poles as required by this section, the mayor shall have power to remove such poles, and the expense of the removal shall be collected in the same manner as delinquent taxes are collected. It shall be the duty of every public utility company to apply to the engineer for directions as to the streets and alleys through which poles are to be placed and the engineer shall also regulate the distance between the poles.
(b) The mayor is hereby authorized and empowered to order the removal of or to remove all unsightly or dangerous poles in Macon-Bibb County, belonging to the several public utility companies. The cost of the removal to be collected as provided in subsection (a). Such removal shall be accomplished within 90 days of notification.
2792: All public utility companies doing business in Macon-Bibb County are hereby required to place on each pole six feet above the base thereof a metal tag with the name of the company to which the pole belongs stamped thereon.
2793: For the purpose of reaching the premises of users of electric service furnished by any company or person operating within Macon-Bibb County under a franchise therefrom, the necessary poles for the service shall be placed at the expense of the company or the person to the property line of the consumer.
2794: It shall be unlawful for any person to remove from the streets or sidewalks of Macon-Bibb County any telegraph, telephone, or other poles so as to leave any part of the pole exposed above the surface of the street or sidewalk.
2795:
With the exception hereinafter referred to and described, all poles shall be removed in the following manner:
(1) Where that portion of the sidewalk or street from which the pole is to be removed has not been paved, the pole shall be taken from the ground and the hole from which it is so taken shall be filled and the dirt placed therein securely packed so as to avoid settling.
(2) When the portion of sidewalk or street from which the pole is to be taken is paved, the pole shall be removed and repaired to the satisfaction of the Macon-Bibb County engineer. The pole shall be removed in its entirety and the resulting hole in the pavement shall be repaired with the same kind of material as that surrounding it.
(3) No holes shall be left unfilled unless barricades are placed to ensure the safety of the public. Final repairs shall be made within 30 days of the pole removal.
2796: Public utility companies shall maintain underground power on those streets in the urban core that currently have underground power. Underground utilities shall not be converted to overhead power without approval of the Macon-Bibb County commission.
2797:
All persons to whom permission may be granted for renewing or laying underground conduits, tubes, or pipes for electrical conductors, cables, or wires, shall conform to the following requirements:
(1) No streets shall be broken or occupied by any person for the purpose of laying down conduits, tubes, or pipes for electrical conductors, cables, or wires, except by written permission of the engineer.
(2) During the construction or laying down of the underground conduits, tubes, or pipes, conductors, cables, or wires, no streets shall be opened or the pavement broken for a greater distance than 500 feet at any one opening, and no section of the 500 feet shall be kept open for a longer period than ten days, and the opening shall not be of greater width than four feet except where permitted by the Macon-Bibb County engineer.
(3) As the work progresses the pavement shall be properly relaid and the street put in good condition.
2798: Prior to making any opening in any street, for the laying of conduits, tubes, or pipes for electrical conductors, cables, or wires, the person desiring to lay the same shall make application to the Macon-Bibb County engineer, in writing, and shall file plans and specifications showing the location, the route, and the length of the proposed conduits, pipes, and tubes. The engineer shall have authority to issue the necessary permit for the opening of the street, as set forth in the application and plans. The opening of the street, without a permit having been first obtained, shall forfeit the right of any person to use or occupy the street. The work of laying any underground conduits, tubes, pipes, electrical conductors, cables, and wires shall be under the direction and approval of the Macon-Bibb County engineer, who shall at all times have free and unobstructed access to the conduits, tubes, pipes, electrical conductors, or cables, for the purpose of inspecting the same, or making connections therewith for wires or conductors in use or to be used by Macon-Bibb County.
2799: It shall be unlawful for any person, except employees of a telephone, telegraph, or electric light or power company, acting under orders, to cut a wire or alter its position without the knowledge or consent of the Macon-Bibb County engineer.
2800: Any person placing conduits under the foregoing provisions shall furnish to Macon-Bibb County on demand one duct in the same location for governmental purposes, without charge, provided no electric light or power wire shall be used in a telephone or telegraph conduit.
2801: All persons having telegraph, telephone, or electric wires, electrical conductors, or cables placed underground shall, in writing on or before January first of each year, report under oath to the mayor and to the Macon-Bibb County commission the actual number of wires, the location, and the miles of wire and electrical conductors underground, owned or leased or controlled by that person in Macon-Bibb County.
2802: Should any person, to whom the right of franchise has heretofore been or shall hereafter be granted to lay underground wires, electrical conductors, cables, or tubes, dispose of such right of franchise, or lease to, consolidate, or merge with any other company, corporation, firm, or person, without first obtaining permission of the mayor and commission to so dispose of or lease, consolidate, or merge, the person shall forfeit all franchise rights and privileges granted.
2803:

(b) A sufficient indemnity bond, certificate of liability insurance, or other approved security shall be given, subject to the approval of the mayor, at the time of granting permission for the underground activities, in the minimum sum of $10,000.00 to cover such damage, and save Macon-Bibb County harmless.
(c) The access agreement issued under section 29-1(e) shall also specify that the holder of an access agreement shall at all times be responsible to the public and hold the city harmless for any property damage or personal injury caused or occasioned by the installation, maintenance or occupancy of any wire, cable or conduit under, upon or above a street or highway right-of-way as permitted in this article.

2807:

(6) The Georgia Power Company, its successors, lessees, and assigns, shall further, in constructing and maintaining its system of overhead lines, poles, wires and other structures, submit and be subject to all laws, rules, and regulations of Macon-Bibb County for the regulation or control of such structures.

2811:

(b) In constructing, laying, maintaining, repairing, replacing, enlarging, and extending its pipes, mains, and necessary accessories in the streets and other public places, the company shall be subject to, and comply with, all ordinances, rules, and regulations of Macon-Bibb County, now or hereafter in force applicable to the use of streets and other public places.
(c) No excavations or work shall be done by Atlanta Gas Light Company in the streets or other places of Macon-Bibb County until a permit has been applied for by the company and granted by the official of Macon-Bibb County charged with that duty, except in emergencies, when the permit shall be obtained for the emergency work at the earliest practicable time. No permit shall be refused where the request is made in conformity to the general ordinances, rules, and regulations of the government and the purpose for which the permit is desired is not in violation of the general ordinances, rules, and regulations nor in violation of the terms of this article.
(d) In addition to complying with all ordinances, rules and regulations of Macon-Bibb County, where the use of the public streets and other public places are involved, the company shall at all times be subject to and comply with all other ordinances, rules and regulations of Macon-Bibb County enacted or promulgated under the police powers of Macon-Bibb County for the safety and protection of the general public.
2812: If any streets, roads, rights-of-way, or other public places owned by Macon-Bibb County or any water lines or mains or sanitary sewer lines or mains owned by Macon-Bibb County water and sewerage authority necessitating the removal or relocation of the Atlanta Gas Light Company facilities located therein in the furtherance of any governmental purpose, the removal or relocation shall be done by Atlanta Gas Light Company at its expense after reasonable notice, provided that the foregoing provisions of this section shall not be applicable where the street alteration or abandonment is done for the convenience of another public utility, whether publicly or privately owned, or for the convenience of any abutting landowner or any governmental agency.
2813: Atlanta Gas Light Company shall be entitled to charge for gas furnished by it, any rates as are prescribed by the public service commission or other lawful regulatory body of the state.
2814:
(a) Atlanta Gas Light Company hereby agrees and covenants, for and in consideration of the rights and privileges herein granted to it, to pay, within 60 days following the end of each quarterly period, Macon-Bibb County three percent of the gas sales receipts received by Atlanta Gas Light Company from residential and commercial, but not industrial customers, within the territorial limits of Macon-Bibb County during the preceding quarterly period (hereinafter referred to as the quarterly period), provided, however, that should Macon-Bibb County require Atlanta Gas Light Company to pay any license fee or tax, excise tax, indirect tax, occupation tax, franchise tax, privilege tax, regulation charge or related fees, these taxes or charges shall be deducted in full by Atlanta Gas Light Company from the quarterly payment or payments subsequently accruing to Macon-Bibb County. The quarterly periods for which these payments shall be made shall commence upon the first day of the month immediately following proper adoption and approval of this article [May 27, 1975]. The commission, through its authorized representative or representatives, shall have the right to inspect and audit the books and records of Atlanta Gas Light Company for the purpose of determining the amount of its revenues received from the sale of gas to residential and commercial, but not industrial customers within Macon-Bibb County limits.
(b) "Industrial gas" or "gas sold to industrial customers," as to which Atlanta Gas Light Company shall pay no part of its revenue to Macon-Bibb County hereunder, is defined to be gas sold to manufacturing, assembling and processing businesses such as textile, and cotton mills, brick and tile manufacturers, glass manufacturing plants, cement plants, foundries, electric generating plants, steel and other metal plants, cotton oil mills, ice plants, bottling plants and other manufacturing plants, automobile and other assembling plants, kaolin processing plants, rubber processing plants, meat packing plants, laundries, bakeries, dairies, food processing plants, and other processing plants; and gas sold to governmental and institutional customers consuming more than 150,000 cubic feet of natural gas on any one-day during the customer's contract year and billed on an interruptible rate schedule, or under a special contract filed with the Georgia Public Service Commission, (or any successor state regulatory group).
2815: Should Atlanta Gas Light Company have in force on and after August 17, 1979, a contract to pay and actually be paying to any other municipality in the state receiving gas service under the same rates and similar conditions as those in effect at that particular time in Macon-Bibb County, a percentage greater than the three percent set out in this article, the three percent shall be increased to such greater percent, which greater percent shall become effective with the commencement of the next following quarterly period and remain effective so long, and only so long, as the Atlanta Gas Light Company shall pay the greater percent to another municipality.
2816: All excavations, construction, repair and other work done by any company in the streets or other public places of Macon-Bibb County shall be at the expense of the company, and all parts of streets and other public places shall be restored by the company so as to leave them in the same condition as before such acts on the part of the company, subject however to existing or future provisions of this Code which may provide that the restoration or replacement of pavement shall be done by Macon-Bibb County at the reasonable cost thereof to be borne by the company. The company shall compensate Macon-Bibb County for all damage to streets and other public places caused by acts or omissions of the company in making excavations, and in constructing, laying, maintaining, repairing, replacing, enlarging and extending the company's pipes, mains and other accessories.
2817: Atlanta Gas Light Company shall save and keep harmless Macon-Bibb County from any and all liability by reason of damage or injury to any person or persons whomsoever, on account of negligence, wrongful act or omission, of Atlanta Gas Light Company in the installation, maintenance and repair of its mains and pipe lines along said streets, avenues, roads, public highways, alleys, lanes, ways, parks and other public places in Macon-Bibb County, provided the Atlanta Gas Light Company shall have been notified in writing of any claim against Macon-Bibb County on account thereof and shall have been given ample opportunity to defend the same.
2818: Any franchise granted hereunder shall not be transferred, assigned or otherwise alienated except with the express consent of Macon-Bibb County; provided, however, that the franchisee shall have the full right and power to transfer the franchise in connection with any merger, consolidation or reorganization of the franchisee or as a part of securing the payment of any indebtedness now existing or hereafter created by the franchisee, its successors or assigns, with or without the consent of Macon-Bibb County. Each and every right and obligation of Atlanta Gas Light Company contained in this article shall extend and apply to its successors and assigns, and wherever Atlanta Gas Light Company is used herein it shall be construed to contain a specific reference to such successors and assigns.
2820:
Base year means the fiscal year ending September 30, 1998.
Base year franchise fee factor means the total franchise fees paid during the base year divided by the design day capacity as recorded by Atlanta Gas Light Company on the last day of the base year.
Design day capacity means the sum of the individual capacity in dekatherms (Dt) attributable to all firm customers located within the geographic limits of Macon-Bibb County as of the last day of the previous fiscal year.
Firm customers means all residential and business customers who purchase gas service that ordinarily is not subject to interruption or curtailment.
Fiscal year means the 12 months ending September 30 of each year.
Inflation index means the percentage change in the consumer price index for all urban consumers as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, or any successor index, for the period from September 30, 1997, to the beginning of the then current fiscal year. The percentage shall be reduced by any productivity factor adjustment for the same time period determined by the state public service commission for Atlanta Gas Light Company.
2821:
The total dollar amount of franchise fees paid by Atlanta Gas Light Company to Macon-Bibb County shall be calculated as follows:
(1) The current fiscal year total franchise fee shall equal the product of the design day capacity and the current franchise fee factor. The current franchise fee factor shall be equal to the product of the base year franchise fee factor and one plus the inflation index expressed as a decimal to three significant digits.
(2) The following formula quantifies this payment:
FFc = FFFby × (1 + (CPI − PFA)) × DDc
Where FFc = total franchise fees due the city for the current fiscal year
FFFby = the base year franchise fee factor
CPI - PFA = the inflation index based on the cumulative change in the consumer price index less the productivity factor adjustment determined by the Georgia Public Service Commission.
DDCc = the design day capacity as of the last day of the previous fiscal year.
FFFby = FFby/DDCby where
FFby = the total franchise fees paid in the base year
and DDCby = the design day capacity of the base year.

2842: Whenever the board of commissioners of Macon-Bibb County shall create a drainage and/or paving district, it shall do so by a resolution which shall define the limits of such drainage and/or paving district and any such resolution so establishing such district may by reference to this article incorporate the same therein and this article shall be as much a part of the resolution creating such drainage and/or paving district as if fully set forth therein.
2843:
(a) Any resolution creating a drainage and/or paving district shall constitute a finding that, in the opinion of the board of commissioners of Macon-Bibb County, it is to the interest of the safety, convenience and health of the people residing in such district so established to improve the drainage and the condition of the streets in such district and such district shall thereby be condemned for drainage and paving, and it is hereby ordered that upon the effective date of such a resolution creating such drainage and/or paving district, that the drainage in such district be improved by the installation of storm sewers of adequate size, and that such district be paved with an asphalt surface on an adequate base, together with the necessary grading and incidental work.
(b) The prorata cost of the improvement described, as such portion as provided by section 29-149, as well as the costs provided by sections 29-147 and 29-148, shall be charges against the respective owners of the properties affected by the improvement and a continuing lien from the date of the resolution creating such special drainage and/or paving district to the date of full payment, against all of the properties of such owners whether affected by the improvements or not, the board of commissioners having the right and power, for and in behalf of Macon-Bibb County, to make collection from such owners or to pursue and subject for payment the properties affected by such improvements or any and all other properties of such owners.
2844: Such improvements shall be done in whole or in part by Macon-Bibb County forces or by contract as then existing conditions may dictate and be determined by the Macon-Bibb County engineer, with the approval and consent of the governing body. It is therefore ordered that such work shall be so accomplished, and the clerk of the Macon-Bibb County commission shall be authorized and directed, as to that portion of work to be accomplished by contract, to advertise for bids for furnishing all labor and materials for doing such work, as required by law.
2845: Such work shall be done in accord with plans and specifications prepared and/or approved by the Macon-Bibb County engineer, and subject to the approval of the Macon-Bibb County commission, and the work shall be performed under the supervision and direction of the Macon-Bibb County engineer.
2846: The clerk of the Macon-Bibb County board of commissioners shall cause to be published at least twice before work is commenced under this article, in the official advertising organ of Macon-Bibb County, notice of the passage of the resolution, and of the intention of Macon-Bibb County to cause the described work to commence and be completed. Such notice shall also advise that any owner of property or other person affected by the proposed work, may within ten days after the last published notice, appeal to the Macon-Bibb County commission and show cause, if any he has, why such proposed work should not be done, such persons being heard upon any material or pertinent matter, affecting the validity or reasonableness of such work, and the manner and means by which it is to be accomplished.
2847: Whenever the Macon-Bibb County engineer shall notify the owners of properties abutting on any district coming under this article or of any area where a drainage and paving project will occur, to move all water meters and lower all water and gas connections, or sewer connections, necessary to the proper construction of such drainage and paving project, each property owner shall immediately have all connections adjusted according to the plans and to the satisfaction of the engineer, and should the property owner within ten days after receiving such notice, fail to have such connections properly adjusted, or notify the engineer in writing that he does not intend to have such adjustments made, the Macon-Bibb County engineer will have adjustments made, and the cost of same, plus a $15.00 charge for handling shall be added to the assessments against the properties or owners and collected in the same manner as the original assessment, and whenever the engineer shall notify the public utility companies having utilities within the districts or adjacent to any planned drainage and paving project to move, lower or adjust such utilities as may be necessary to the proper construction of such drainage and paving project, the utility companies shall immediately have all utilities adjusted according to the plans and to the satisfaction of the Macon-Bibb County engineer. Such notice may be served either by leaving same at the residence of the respective property owners or at the office of the respective utilities or by depositing the same in the U.S. mail enclosed in an envelope properly stamped and addressed to the owner. Such notice shall also advise that any person affected may within five days of the date of such notice, appeal to the Macon-Bibb County commission for an extension of time for completing such work directed in such notice.
2848: Whenever, in the opinion of the Macon-Bibb County engineer, there shall exist artificial obstructions within or upon the areas of the right-of-way to be improved or needed as work area for the improvement, he shall notify the property owner whose property abuts the portion of the right-of-way so obstructed to remove such obstructions within ten days of the receipt of such notice and upon failure to do so Macon-Bibb County will remove the same without responsibility or liability therefor, and will charge and assess the entire cost of such removal against the property and owner affected in all instances where the obstructions have been created or maintained by such property owner. The notice provided for in this section shall be served and an appeal allowed as provided in section 29-147.
2849: Immediately upon the completion of any drainage and/or paving improvement made in any area of Macon-Bibb County, the Macon-Bibb County engineer shall certify to the Macon-Bibb County commission that the work of drainage and paving has been completed; and thereupon it shall become the duty of the commission to assess the cost of the work as follows: The real estate abutting on each side of such drainage and/or paving project shall be assessed and shall together pay two-thirds of the entire cost, including the drainage, each piece of real estate to be assessed in proportion that the frontage of such realty bears to the entire frontage so paved and/or drained as by law provided. In determining the entire cost of such work to be proportionally assessed, the commission shall have the right to include the cost of construction, replacement, or repair of steps, driveways, or lateral walks whether or not situated within the right-of-way, where in the judgment of the commission, the same are necessary to ingress and egress to and from abutting property.
2850:
(a) Immediately after the cost of paving and/or draining under this article shall have been prorated and assessed by the Macon-Bibb County commission, the Macon-Bibb County engineer shall prepare a list of the property owners whose property abuts on the paving and/or drainage project and provide it to the Macon-Bibb County tax commissioner who shall mail to the property owners a written notice or statement of the amount so assessed in a properly addressed and stamped envelope. Thereupon each property owner shall make payment for such paving and drainage so assessed against each respectively within 30 days from the date of such notice unless the board of commissioners shall have determined that extenuating circumstances exist. If the board of commissioners in its sole discretion determines that extenuating circumstances exist, the board may permit the property owners to pay the assessment in monthly or quarterly installments over a term not to exceed five years. In such instance, the written notice or statement shall be mailed to the property owners as required herein immediately after approval of the installment payment and term and the property owners shall make such payments each month during the approved term until such assessment shall have been paid in full.
(b) In the event that any property owner shall fail to pay the Macon-Bibb County tax commissioner his assessment within 30 days from the date of such notice, or in the case where payment is approved in monthly or quarterly installments as set forth in subsection (a), each month or quarter during the approved payment term, then the Macon-Bibb County board of commissioners or its designated agent shall issue an execution against such delinquent property owner for the amount due and unpaid, together with all costs thereon, and each execution shall bear interest at the rate then in effect and applicable to executions for delinquent ad valorem taxes; provided, however, that in computing interest, a fraction of a month shall be charged as a full month. Any property owner failing to pay the tax commissioner his assessment within the time provided for in this section shall pay, in addition to the principal amount, such interest as is currently applicable from time to time.
(c) The execution issued by the Macon-Bibb County board of commissioners or its designated agent, as provided for in this section shall bind and be a lien upon all property of such delinquent owner abutting on such improvements or served thereby and shall be a special lien superior to all other liens except for taxes upon such property. The execution shall be collected and defenses thereto may be made in the manner provided by law with respect to ad valorem taxes.
2851: The action taken in this article and the method provided for the collection of the assessments shall be cumulative of all rights of Macon-Bibb County otherwise afforded by law, including any and all contracts and petitions of property owners for the paving and drainage.
2852: Any errors made in the assessments provided for in this article may be corrected at any time by reassessment.
2854:
This section and the following sections, through and including section 29-165, provide for the means by which there may be created and established special districts for the acquisition of all necessary easements for, and construction and installation of, all infrastructure necessary to provide sewerage for sanitary sewage conveyance services to properties within said districts, and to provide a means of funding therefor through fees, assessments, and taxes that may be levied and collected within such districts to pay, wholly or partially, the cost thereof. These sections of this Code may be collectively referred to as the "Special Sanitary Sewerage District Ordinance."
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2855:
The special districts shall be created for the following purposes:
To provide a means funding acquisition of all necessary easements for, and construction, and installation of, all infrastructure necessary to provide sewerage for sanitary sewage conveyance services to properties within the special districts.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2856:
(a) When sanitary sewage conveyance services are desired by residents and property owners of an existing neighborhood or subdivision that received final plat approval at least two (2) years prior to the submission of the application fee described in subsection (b), those residents and property owners may, by application submitted to the Board of Commissioners, request the creation of a special district to fund the construction and installation of all infrastructure necessary to provide the services throughout the following procedure:
(b) The application referred to in subsection (a), forms for which will be available from the Macon Water Authority, shall be signed by the owners of more than fifty percent (50%) of the lots in the requesting neighborhood or subdivision and shall be accompanied by a non-refundable application fee equal to one hundred dollars ($100.00) multiplied by one-half (½) the number of lots in the development to be served by the special district, but in no event shall the application fee be less than twenty-five hundred dollars ($2,500.00). The Clerk shall verify that the application and fee satisfy the criteria set forth in this subsection.
(c) If the application and fee satisfy the criteria set forth in subsection (b), the Clerk shall deliver the fee and a copy of the application to the Macon Water Authority with a request that the Macon Water Authority conduct a feasibility study to determine the appropriate boundaries of the special district, to prepare a plat showing the proposed special district, to estimate the cost of providing sewer service to the district including but not limited to engineering, easement acquisition, construction, construction observation, permits, and debt service, to estimate the necessary millage rate for the special district and the number of years the district must exist to provide the funding for the project, and to render an opinion as to whether the project is otherwise appropriate for a special district. The Macon Water Authority will deliver a copy of the report of the feasibility study to the Board of Commissioners and to each applicant whose signature appears on the application. The Macon Water Authority may retain the application fee to help defray the cost of the feasibility study and dissemination thereof.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2857:
Following dissemination of the report of the feasibility study as aforesaid, the Board of Commissioners shall conduct a public hearing for the purpose of determining whether or not to create the proposed special district, giving consideration to the report, to the comments by interested members of the public, and any other health, safety, and welfare concerns. The public hearing shall be advertised one (1) time in the official organ of the County; and at least one (1) sign shall be posted in the proposed special district giving notice of the hearing, at least fifteen (15) days before the public hearing.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2858:
Following the public hearing, the Board of Commissioners shall determine by a majority vote whether to accept a petition, from owners of the property within the boundaries of the proposed district as described by the report of the feasibility study, to establish a special district fitting the criteria specified in the report of the feasibility study. If the Board of Commissioners vote to accept a petition, the Board of Commissioners may establish a deadline by which the petition must be submitted.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2859:
If the owners of sixty-five percent (65%) of the lots in the proposed special district sign the petition for the creation of a special district conforming to the criteria set forth in the report of the feasibility study, the Board of Commissioners shall declare that the district is created. Once created, the district shall continue to exist until the cost of the project and the indebtedness of the Macon Water Authority for the completion of the project is retired. A plat describing the district shall be filed with Clerk of the County Superior Court and the County Engineer. Plats shall also be available to the public for inspection at the Macon Water Authority and at the offices of the Board of Commissioners.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2860:
Whenever a special district is created, the County shall enter into a contract with the Macon Water Authority for the construction of the project. The contact shall include a statement of the scope of the project, and shall provide that responsibility for funding and managing the project shall belong to the Macon Water Authority. The contract shall provide that upon completion of the project, title to the infrastructure and any necessary easements shall be in the name of the Macon Water Authority. It shall further provide that responsibility for the maintenance of the completed sewer infrastructure shall belong to Macon Water Authority. It shall further provide that the assessments collected in the special district will be paid over to the Macon Water Authority to fund the full cost of the project, to reimburse the County for its costs and expenses incurred in performing its responsibilities set forth in Sections 29-155 through 29-158 with respect to the special district, and to retire any indebtedness incurred by the Macon Water Authority to fund the project. The contract shall contain a commitment obligating the Board of Commissioners to utilize all reasonable means, including but not limited to execution, levy, foreclosure, and sale, to collect any delinquent assessments imposed pursuant to this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance. If the project as proposed includes excess capacity, the contrast shall include a statement explaining how any basin specific fee would be established and how said fees would offset the construction cost owed by the special district.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2861:
The Board of Commissioners shall establish an annual assessment to be imposed upon each of the lots in the district. Payment of the first assessment shall be due concurrently with the due date for payment of ad valorem taxes for the calendar year in which the district is created. Payment shall be due annually thereafter until the cost of the project and the indebtedness of the Macon Water Authority for the completion of the project are retired. The office of the Tax Commissioner shall be responsible for the collection of the assessments for each special district.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2862:
In addition to any other rights of collection for late or unpaid charges, the County shall have the rights available under the laws of the State for assessment, including the creation of a lien upon the property the assessment for which is not timely paid, together with all rights of execution, levy, foreclosure, and sale.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2863:
No part of the assessments collected in the special district shall be used to defray the cost of connecting to installed sewerage infrastructure. All such costs shall be borne by property owners' who desire to make such connection, in accordance with policies and practices of the Macon Water Authority in effect from time to time. Connection to the infrastructure is not required as a condition of the establishment of the district, but every property against which assessments are made shall have the right to connect to the infrastructure, in accordance with said policies and practices of the Macon Water Authority.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2864:
If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, or phrase of this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance is, for any reason, held to be invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2865:
If any provision of this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance is in conflict with any state or federal law, or with any rule, regulation, or order of any agency of this state or federal agency having jurisdiction of the subject matter of this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance, it is hereby deemed to be the intention of the Board of Commissioners that the state or federal law or rule, regulation, or order, as the case may be, shall prevail so that the remaining portion of this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance shall be deemed to be of full force and effect.
(Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)
2866:
If the intent of this Special Sanitary Sewerage District ordinance to protect the public health, safety, and general welfare of all properties and persons in general, but not to create any special duty or relationship with any individual person or to any specified property within or without the unincorporated boundaries of the County. (Ord. No. O-14-0045, § 1, 8-19-2014)

2869: No person shall hereafter lay any water pipe or main, gas pipe or main, or any other main upon any part of the public streets or highways within Macon-Bibb County without first having obtained a permit therefor from the Macon-Bibb County engineer as provided in section 29-2.
2870: No such pipe or main shall be laid upon any such street or highway unless the same is at least 30 inches below the grade of such street or highway, and any pipe so laid shall be upon condition that the same will be changed wholly at the expense of the property owner or applicant, to conform to any new grade which may be hereafter established for the street or highway on which it is located, so as to be at all times at least 30 inches below the grade of such street or highway.
2871: The owners or users of any mains or pipes now existing within the area of Macon-Bibb County are permitted to continue the use of such highways only on condition that such mains or pipes now are, or shall be within 30 days of the direction of the Macon-Bibb County engineer as needed to protect the existing road and drainage system, placed at least 30 inches below present grade, and upon the change of grade in any such highway hereafter, such owner or users will likewise be required at his own expense to adjust such mains or pipes so that they at all times will be at least 30 inches below the grade of such highway.
2872: Before the Macon-Bibb County engineer shall issue to any person a permit to lay any water, gas, sewer pipe or any other pipe or conduit on any public road or street of Macon-Bibb County which is paved in such a manner as to necessitate the disturbing of the pavement, such person shall pay to the Macon-Bibb County engineer an inspection fee to be established by the Macon-Bibb County engineer, which amount is set as the minimum charge for replacing or repairing the pavement damaged by the excavation, and no portion of which shall be returned to the holder of the permit.
2873:
All permits shall be issued and all pipe and conduits shall be installed subject to and in accord with the following conditions and regulations:
(1) No pipe nor conduit shall be installed less than 30 inches deep.
(2) No excavation shall be made under the pavement larger than the hole in the pavement.
(3) The excavation shall be properly backfilled and the backfill material thoroughly tamped into place, the material being left slightly higher than the pavement to allow for settlement, and should settlement occur, the party making the excavation shall keep same filled up with satisfactory material until pavement is repaired.
(4) Adequate barricades, proper signage, and lights shall be provided by the party making the excavation at all times during construction and until pavement is repaired.
(5) Upon completion of construction and the proper filling of the excavation the contractor shall notify the Macon-Bibb County engineer that the work is complete and that the pavement may be repaired.
(6) After, in the opinion of the Macon-Bibb County engineer, sufficient time has elapsed for the backfill to properly settle, the pavement shall be repaired by Macon-Bibb County forces.
(7) No parties other than Macon-Bibb County forces shall repair or replace any pavement without the express consent of the Macon-Bibb County engineer.
(8) No pipe or conduit shall be laid at such a grade or in such a manner as to disturb any existing cross-drain, culvert, pipe, storm sewer, sanitary sewer, side-drain pipe or other existing pipe, nor less than four inches above the top or below the bottom of any existing pipe or culvert.
2874: The Macon-Bibb County engineer shall have prepared proper forms for the applications for permits, and for the permits, and the engineer shall keep a complete and accurate record of all permits issued, all charges made and all payments received.
2875: The Macon-Bibb County engineer is hereby authorized and instructed to remove from the right-of-way of any public road or street, any pipe or conduit which is not installed in accordance with the foregoing regulations or which is installed without a permit having first been obtained even though it be otherwise properly installed, and to replace the roadway in the same condition as it was before the installation.
2876: It shall be unlawful for any person to connect to the water lines constructed by the Macon water authority without having previously obtained a permit so to do from the Macon-Bibb County engineer; provided, however, that this section shall not apply to connections for fire suppression lines.
2877: It shall be unlawful for any person to connect to a water line belonging to the Macon water authority without having installed a water meter for the purpose of measuring the water consumed through the tap so made; provided, however, that this section shall not apply to connections for fire suppression lines.
2878: It shall be unlawful for any person to tamper with any meter installed by the Macon water authority or by the former board of water commissioners of the City of Macon so as to render it inoperable, or otherwise impair its proper operation.
2879: It shall be unlawful for any person to install any water service line or to alter any previously installed water service line so as to cause the same to bypass any meter located upon a service line which itself is connected with a water line owned by the Macon water authority.
2880: It shall be unlawful for any person owning or occupying business or residential premises to permit the consumption of water upon such premises, if such water has been obtained through the water system operated by or for the account of the Macon water authority, unless such water so consumed has passed through a water meter in good operating condition which accurately measures the amount of water passing through such meter; provided, however, that this section shall not apply to fire suppression lines.
2881: It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to pay, promptly when due, any bills for water consumed or for other charges rendered by the Macon water authority, or by its agent.
2882: It shall be unlawful for any person to do any act or to omit to do any act whether or not specifically hereinabove set forth which results in the failure of such person to pay any sums of money due to the Macon water authority, or to its agent for the account of the authority which are properly due and owing.
2883: Each day that any such person remains in violation of this resolution [chapter] shall constitute a separate offense and shall be punishable as such.
2884: Any person charged with the violation of this chapter shall be tried in the municipal court of Macon-Bibb County, and, upon conviction, shall be punished as provided by the laws of the state pertaining to that court except that the penalties and punishment shall be as provided in section 1-6.
2885:
Macon-Bibb County finds that there is an imminent need to foster a culture of water conservation and to plan for water supply enhancement during future extreme drought conditions and other water emergencies; and that reasonable restrictions on the outdoor watering of landscape are necessary in furtherance of addressing this need.
The purposes and intent in enacting sections 29-187 through 29-189 are as follows, and to these ends the said regulations are hereby adopted:
(1) To address outdoor watering of landscape to promote conservation of water and enhance water supply; and
(2) To comply with the mandate of the Georgia General Assembly (Senate Bill 370) that all counties adopt an ordinance limiting outdoor watering of landscape to the hours between 4:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. (with certain exceptions) to take effect not later than January 1, 2011.
(3) This section is enacted pursuant to authority granted under O.C.G.A. § 12-5-7, to regulate the outdoor watering of landscape in Macon-Bibb County.
2887:
(a) No person shall use or allow the use of water in violation of the restrictions on outdoor water use contained in the ordinance from which this section derives.
(b) The Macon water authority shall be the enforcement authority for the ordinance from which this section derives. The Macon-Bibb County board of commissioners may also authorize other departments as may be deemed necessary to support enforcement.
(c) Criminal and alternative penalties. Any violation of this section may also be enforced by a citation returnable to the municipal court or by any other legal means as set forth in this Code.
